articles.headline: Echo Oppn's sentiments to Amit Shah: V-P to Rijiju
articles.summary: Vice-President Jagdeep Dhankhar requested parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju to convey the 'sentiments of the Opposition' to home minister Amit Shah. The move follows continuous disruption in the Rajya Sabha over allegations of police excesses and the use of pellet guns against student protesters in Delhi. The Opposition has demanded a statement from Shah in the House.

articles.headline: Compliance, moderation in focus as Meta, govt hold talks
articles.summary: The Union government and Meta are engaged in discussions regarding the company's content moderation policies and compliance mechanisms. This follows a technical error that led to the temporary removal of a video posted by PM Narendra Modi on Meta's platform. The government is seeking clarity on automated systems and ensuring alignment with Indian constitutional and legal standards.

articles.headline: SA recalls envoy amid Zuma-Gupta meeting furore
articles.summary: South Africa has recalled its high commissioner to India, Anil Sooklal, following reports of a meeting between former president Jacob Zuma and one of the Gupta brothers in Dubai. The move highlights the ongoing sensitivity regarding the state capture allegations involving the Gupta family. Sooklal has been recalled for 'consultations' as the government reviews the diplomatic fallout.

articles.headline: Downpour again clogs NCR; three dead in Gurugram
articles.summary: Heavy rainfall in the National Capital Region led to severe waterlogging and three deaths in Gurugram. Two men died of electrocution and a woman was killed in a balcony collapse. The rain caused major traffic snarls and power outages across Delhi, Gurugram, and Noida. The weather office has issued a yellow alert for Friday with moderate rainfall expected to continue.

articles.headline: SC dismisses last appeal against Bofors acquittal
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed the final surviving appeal against the 2005 Delhi High Court judgment that quashed all criminal proceedings in the Bofors payoff case. The bench quashed the appeal against the acquittal of the Hinduja brothers and Swedish arms manufacturer AB Bofors, citing an 'unconscionable delay' of over 4,500 days in filing the petition by the central government.

articles.headline: SC expands scope of subvention case probe
articles.summary: The Supreme Court expanded the scope of a probe into a major subvention scheme fraud involving top builders and bank officials. The court directed the CBI to share details of alleged proceeds of crime with the Enforcement Directorate. The investigation involves multiple housing projects across Delhi-NCR and Noida where home buyers were allegedly defrauded by builders and banks.

articles.headline: Suvendu aide murder case: CBI charge-sheets 11
articles.summary: The CBI has filed a charge-sheet against 11 individuals, including two BJP workers, in connection with the 2021 murder of a close aide of Bengal LoP Suvendu Adhikari. The victim, Chandranath Rath, was killed in the aftermath of the West Bengal assembly elections. The agency's probe revealed a conspiracy involving political rivals and local criminals to execute the targeted killing.

articles.headline: Kerala man held for Kochi flight emergency exit bid
articles.summary: A passenger on a Kuala Lumpur-Kochi flight was arrested for allegedly attempting to open the aircraft's emergency exit mid-air. The individual, identified as Jamsheer Athannikkal from Palakkad, reportedly damaged the window panel and threatened fellow passengers. He was taken into custody by Kochi police upon landing and booked under various sections of the Aircraft Act for violating safety.

articles.headline: Meaty makeover: Lettuce, tobacco engineered for meat protein
articles.summary: Scientists have successfully engineered lettuce and tobacco plants to produce myoglobin, the protein that gives meat its color, taste, and iron content. Researchers from Imperial College London and other institutions believe this could provide a more realistic and nutrient-rich route for plant-based meat substitutes. The study was published in the journal Frontiers in Plant Science.

articles.headline: Atrophy of the elephant: How BSP lost Uttar Pradesh
articles.summary: A detailed analysis of the Bahujan Samaj Party's (BSP) decline in Uttar Pradesh reveals the party's transition from a dominant force to having zero representation in the state assembly. The shift is attributed to the BJP's rise since 2014, which captured a significant portion of the non-Dalit Hindu vote and fractured the BSP's core social engineering strategy of pragmatic political alliances.

articles.headline: Govt against sub-quotas based solely on income
articles.summary: The Union government informed the Supreme Court that it opposes an income-based sub-quota within the reserved categories for SCs, STs, and OBCs. The Centre argued that reservation is intended to address historical social disadvantage and untouchability, not just economic status. It warned that introducing an income-only criteria would dilute the constitutional purpose of affirmative action.

articles.headline: Delhi Police nab 'doctor' for cop's murder after 3 decades
articles.summary: Delhi Police arrested Rajender Bairagi, a man who allegedly murdered two police officers in 1996 and had been living under a false identity for 28 years. Bairagi, who was working as a physical education teacher in a Mumbai school, was captured following a tip-off. He had escaped from custody in Haryana years ago and is linked to multiple murder and robbery cases across several states.

articles.headline: Viksit Bharat aims to restore India's historical standing: FM
articles.summary: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that the 'Viksit Bharat 2047' vision is designed to restore India's historical economic dominance. Speaking at the C.D. Deshmukh Lecture, she noted that India once accounted for one-third of global GDP before colonial rule. The government aims to reach this level again through qualitative education, comprehensive healthcare, and manufacturing.

articles.headline: We're united: CM Siddaramaiah rejects discontent within Cong
articles.summary: Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah dismissed reports of internal friction in the state Congress unit following cabinet reshuffle rumors. He stated that the party remains united and that any individual grievances are being addressed by the high command. The clarification comes amid speculation that several senior MLAs were unhappy over the selection criteria for ministerial berths and local boards.

articles.headline: Karnataka women association says all-male cabinet not acceptable
articles.summary: The Karnataka Women's Association has protested the lack of female representation in the state's newly expanded cabinet. The group submitted a letter to the Deputy CM, calling it a 'betrayal' of women's leadership and the party's election promises. They noted that despite women being a primary voter base, no ministerial portfolio was allocated to a female legislator in the recent expansion.

articles.headline: LoP takes dig at DKS, calls him dummy CM
articles.summary: BJP leader and Leader of Opposition R. Ashoka criticized Deputy CM D.K. Shivakumar, labeling him a 'dummy CM' who is allegedly being sidelined by the Congress high command. Ashoka claimed that the delay in portfolio allocation and cabinet expansion shows that the state government is being run via 'remote control' from Delhi, leading to a lack of governance in Karnataka.

articles.headline: State govt launches AI-driven digital crop survey initiative
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has launched a technology-driven digital crop survey using satellite imagery, drones, and AI. The project aims to improve the accuracy of crop data for insurance, subsidies, and planning. It integrates several existing systems to provide high-resolution, real-time data to the agriculture department, enabling better policy-making and direct benefit transfers.

articles.headline: DKS unveils plans for 3 Lalbagh-like parks in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Karnataka Deputy CM D.K. Shivakumar announced plans to develop three large botanical gardens in Bengaluru, modeled after the historic Lalbagh. The parks will be located on defense and forest lands in the northern and western parts of the city. The project aims to increase the city's green cover and provide new lung spaces for residents. Forest department approval is currently pending.

articles.headline: Andhra cabinet decides to withdraw Disha Bill
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh cabinet, led by CM N. Chandrababu Naidu, has decided to withdraw the Disha Bill (Criminal Law AP Amendment Bill, 2019). The legislation, introduced by the previous government, aimed to fast-track rape cases and introduce the death penalty. The current government stated that the bill faced constitutional hurdles and that they will focus on existing central criminal laws.

articles.headline: Vijay urges PM to implement project linking 3 major rivers
articles.summary: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) chief Vijay has written to PM Modi requesting the urgent implementation of the project linking the Godavari, Cauvery, and Gundar rivers. He emphasized that the project is a national importance for addressing water scarcity in Tamil Nadu, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh. Vijay urged the Centre to allocate funds and fast-track the execution as a special project.

articles.headline: Andhra records six-fold hike in FDI in last 2 years
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government reported a six-fold increase in Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) over the past two years. According to official data, FDI inflows rose from $92.13 million in FY 2023-24 to over $608.59 million. The government attributed this growth to improved ease of doing business, new industrial policies, and attracting major investments in infrastructure and green energy.

articles.headline: Rs 557 cr spent on PM's foreign visits since 2021
articles.summary: The Union government informed Parliament that Rs 557.51 crore has been spent on PM Narendra Modi's foreign visits to 77 countries since 2021. The highest expenditure was recorded in 2025 at Rs 199.51 crore. The visits resulted in 316 bilateral agreements and MoUs across sectors like trade, investment, defense, and space. Visits to Norway, France, and Australia were among the most expensive.

articles.headline: Need to bolster legal framework to deal with data thefts: SC
articles.summary: The Supreme Court stressed the urgent need for a stronger legal framework to combat large-scale data thefts and cybercrimes in India. The court was hearing a plea regarding the alleged hacking and leak of data of over 150,000 citizens from various portals. The bench noted that existing laws are insufficient for the current digital landscape and urged the government to update legislation.

articles.headline: Houthis kill 38 Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces
articles.summary: In a major escalation in Yemen, Houthi rebels killed 38 Saudi-backed government soldiers in a coordinated missile and drone strike on a military base. The attack comes amid a fragile ceasefire and a buildup of forces near key oil-producing regions. The incident has raised fears of a return to full-scale war in the Arabian Peninsula, threatening regional stability and global energy supplies.

articles.headline: Canada deported over 3,300 Indians in H1 of this year
articles.summary: The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) deported 3,357 Indians in the first six months of this year, a record high. The majority of deportations involved individuals on study and work permits who were found to be involved in organized criminal activities or extortion-related violence in major cities like Toronto and Vancouver. This marks a significant increase compared to previous years.

articles.headline: Life after Ashwin-Jadeja: Do India have spin succession plan?
articles.summary: As senior spinners Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja approach the twilight of their careers, Indian cricket is focusing on finding long-term successors. The team management is testing several young spin options, including Kuldeep Yadav, Axar Patel, and Rahul Chahar, in upcoming tours. The focus is on identifying bowlers who can match the consistency and match-winning ability of the veterans.

articles.headline: Jadumani's silver medal brings golden glow to Manipur boxing
articles.summary: Jadumani Singh won a silver medal in boxing at the Commonwealth Games, sparking celebrations in Manipur. This is the state's first major international boxing medal in several years. The achievement is seen as a revival of Manipur's storied boxing legacy, which has produced several Olympic and world champions. Jadumani's success is expected to inspire a new generation of boxers in the region.

articles.headline: Elon Musk to Build AI Semiconductor Complex in Grimes County, Texas
articles.summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX and Tesla will initially invest $16.8 billion to build 'Terafab,' an advanced AI semiconductor complex in Grimes County, Texas. The facility aims to bolster AI hardware capabilities for both companies.

articles.headline: Bangladesh Asks India To Clarify Policy Towards Dhaka After Hasina Presser
articles.summary: Bangladesh has requested India to clarify its policy stance towards Dhaka following a press conference held by former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. The request highlights diplomatic tensions and the need for clear bilateral communication.

articles.headline: Watchdog Fines Seven Companies For Hidden Drip Pricing Charges Online
articles.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority fined seven companies, including Zepto, PhysicsWallah, and FirstCry, for using 'dark patterns' like drip pricing and basket sneaking. Total penalties reached several lakhs for misleading consumers.

articles.headline: Karnataka Government Mulls Introducing Reservation Quotas For Rural School Students
articles.summary: The Karnataka government is considering a separate reservation for rural government school students in professional course admissions. Currently, students from both government and private rural schools are eligible for a 15% CET quota.

articles.headline: Former India Pacer Vinay Kumar To Return As Karnataka Head Coach
articles.summary: Former Indian pacer Vinay Kumar is set to become the head coach of the Karnataka senior men’s cricket team. The 42-year-old received approval from the Cricket Administrative Committee, which includes Anil Kumble and Rahul Dravid.

articles.headline: New US Rules May Affect Holders Of Long-Term Immigration Visas
articles.summary: USCIS has restored officers' discretion to deny immigration benefit requests without first issuing a 'Request for Evidence.' This move could create challenges for long-term visa holders, such as H-1B applicants, who lack clear proof of eligibility.

articles.headline: Uttarakhand Poll Body Issues Notices To CEO and Three BJP MLAs
articles.summary: The Uttarakhand Chief Electoral Officer and three BJP lawmakers have been served notices by the opposition leader regarding errors in the Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls, including spelling mistakes and unupdated addresses.

articles.headline: Over 5.7 Lakh People Fined For Public Smoking Across India
articles.summary: Data released in the Rajya Sabha reveals that over 5.7 lakh people were fined for smoking in public across India during 2025-26. Authorities collected over Rs 5.1 crore in penalties, though some states reported zero violations or fines.

articles.headline: Gujarat Village Produces 17 Fide-Rated Chess Players In Four Years
articles.summary: Ratusinh Na Muvada, a small village in Gujarat, has produced 17 FIDE-rated chess players in just four years thanks to a local movement started by a math teacher. The village now hosts a dedicated chess hall to train aspiring players.

articles.headline: Survey Shows 81 Percent Of Study-Abroad Aspirants Plan To Return Home
articles.summary: A global survey of 17,925 students indicates that 81% of Indian students studying abroad plan to return to India after completing their courses. Family influence and improved local career prospects were cited as primary drivers for the decision.

articles.headline: Disability Certificate Not Mandatory For PwBD Quota MBBS Seats Says NMC
articles.summary: The National Medical Commission (NMC) clarified that candidates can apply for MBBS seats under the PwBD quota even if they only hold a temporary disability certificate. Eligibility will be determined by assessment centers before counseling.

articles.headline: Canadian Intel Reports Lawrence Gang Using Student Visas For Expansion
articles.summary: Canadian security agencies report that the Lawrence Bishnoi gang is exploiting student visas and work permits to expand extortion operations in British Columbia and Ontario. The gang reportedly targets businesses within South Asian communities.

articles.headline: Alternative Fuel Passenger Vehicles Market Share Gains On Petrol Models
articles.summary: Non-petrol passenger vehicles, including CNG, hybrids, and EVs, accounted for 40.6% of retail sales in July. Petrol's market share dropped to 41.7% as consumers increasingly shift toward vehicles with lower running costs and greener fuel options.

articles.headline: Home Minister Shah Assures Mizoram CM On No Retro FCRA Clause
articles.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah assured Mizoram CM Lalduhoma that proposed amendments to the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) will not apply retrospectively. This assurance follows concerns from NGOs and religious organizations about past funding.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Refuses To Stop Investigation Against Defaulting Realty Builders
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that real estate builders who default on projects cannot stop ongoing police or CBI investigations simply by settling with a few homebuyers. The court emphasized the need for a thorough probe into the allegations of fraud.

articles.headline: RBI Permits Locking Defaulters Mobile Devices To Recover EMIs
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has eased norms to allow lenders to remotely lock the mobile devices of borrowers who default on EMI payments for gadgets. The move aims to improve recovery rates for small-ticket consumer loans.

articles.headline: CJP To Launch National Outreach Campaign For Education And Jobs
articles.summary: The Chhatrapati Janta Party (CJP) announced a nationwide outreach campaign starting in September to address issues of education, unemployment, and governance. The campaign aims to connect directly with citizens and influence future electoral policies.

articles.headline: Bhawana Kanth Becomes India's First Woman To Earn 'Top Gun' Title
articles.summary: Squadron Leader Bhawana Kanth has made history by successfully clearing the 'Top Gun' combat pilot course. She is the first Indian woman to earn this prestigious title, marking a significant milestone for women in the Indian Air Force.

articles.headline: Tata And Adani Groups Submit Nuclear Power Plant Proposals To Odisha
articles.summary: The Tata and Adani groups have submitted separate proposals to the Odisha government to set up nuclear power plants in the state. The government is currently evaluating the development and energy security aspects of the multi-billion dollar projects.

articles.headline: Trump Criticizes Hegseth Over Report On Dwindling US Munitions Arsenal
articles.summary: Donald Trump reportedly criticized his defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, following reports that US munitions stocks have dwindled to dangerously low levels. Trump questioned why the inventory was depleted and accused leakers of spreading misinformation.

articles.headline: Bike-Taxi Crackdown In Bengaluru Leads To Higher Auto Fares For Commuters
articles.summary: A recent crackdown on illegal bike-taxi operations by Bengaluru transport officials has caused a shortage of last-mile transport options. Consequently, auto-rickshaw drivers have significantly increased fares, leaving many commuters stranded or overcharged.

articles.headline: Bengaluru Gig Workers Face Battery Shortages For Electric Delivery Vehicles
articles.summary: Electric bike-taxi and food delivery workers in Bengaluru are struggling with a shortage of charged batteries at swapping stations. Many report losing work hours and income as they wait for hours to replace depleted batteries for their vehicles.

articles.headline: Night Flybus Service From Bengaluru To Kozhikode To Start Aug 15
articles.summary: The KSRTC will launch a direct night Flybus service connecting Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru to Kozhikode starting August 15. The service is designed to provide convenient overnight travel for air passengers heading to North Kerala.

articles.headline: Bengaluru Metro's Pink Line And Airport Connectivity Prioritized By New MD
articles.summary: The new BMRCL MD, Jaffer, announced that completing the Pink Line and the 58km Silk Board-to-Airport stretch are top priorities. Efforts are being made to expedite construction and signaling to meet upcoming deadlines for both metro corridors.

articles.headline: High Court Directs Karnataka Government To Submit Hebbal Tunnel Impact Report
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court has ordered the state government to submit a detailed report on the hydrological and environmental impact of the proposed Hebbal tunnel project. The court warned that the project could be stayed if the report is not filed within 10 days.

articles.headline: Drunk Corporate Designer Arrested After Firing Airgun From Balcony In Bengaluru
articles.summary: A 37-year-old senior designer was arrested in Bengaluru after firing an airgun from his apartment balcony during a 40-minute rampage. The suspect, reportedly under the influence of alcohol, fired several shots into a car and a parking lot.

articles.headline: Jewellery Store Owner In Bengaluru Fights Off Armed Robbers During Heist
articles.summary: The owner of a jewelry store at Dobbespet fought off two armed robbers who entered his shop posing as customers. Despite being shot in the leg, the owner threw items at the miscreants, forcing them to flee without any stolen goods.

articles.headline: Karnataka High Court Orders Suspension Of Medical Professor For Student Abuse
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court ordered the suspension of a medical professor at Shimoga Institute of Medical Sciences for the alleged sexual harassment of girl students. The court criticized the state for previously shielding the accused and revoked his current posting.

articles.headline: Bengaluru Authorities Clear 35 Encroachments On Vijayanagar Food Street
articles.summary: The Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) cleared 35 illegal structures encroaching upon a 250-metre stretch of the Vijayanagar Food Street. The action followed complaints about restricted pedestrian movement and unauthorized food vendors.

articles.headline: Bengaluru CM Plans Three New Mega Parks To Increase Urban Greenery
articles.summary: Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah announced plans to develop three large parks in Bengaluru to expand the city's green cover. The parks, modeled after Cubbon Park and Lalbagh, will be located in different parts of the city to provide more recreational spaces.

articles.headline: Travel Time Reduced By 50 Percent At Kaggadasapura Railway Crossing
articles.summary: A new traffic management experiment at the Kaggadasapura railway crossing in Bengaluru has reduced travel times by 50-60%. Officials used barriers and lane dividers to prevent wrong-way driving, significantly easing congestion during peak hours.

articles.headline: CBSE and ICSE Students Secure Half Of Karnataka Rural Seats: Report
articles.summary: A report reveals that students from CBSE and ICSE schools have secured nearly half of the MBBS seats reserved for rural students in Karnataka. This has sparked a debate over whether the 15% rural quota should be limited to government school students.

articles.headline: Woman In Bengaluru Ends Life After Alleged Harassment Over Failed Investment
articles.summary: A 56-year-old woman committed suicide after she was reportedly harassed and humiliated by individuals following a failed Rs 4-crore real estate investment. The family alleges the accused cheated her and threatened her before she took the extreme step.

articles.headline: Man Arrested For Killing Wife And Hiding Body In Bedroom
articles.summary: Bengaluru police arrested a 24-year-old factory worker for allegedly killing his wife and hiding her body in a bedsheet inside their rented room. The crime was discovered after neighbors reported a foul smell emanating from the locked house.

articles.headline: Congress Moves To Placate Senior Leaders Over Karnataka Cabinet Berth Fallout
articles.summary: The Congress leadership in Karnataka is working to address discontent among senior MLAs who were overlooked in the recent cabinet expansion. Measures include potential appointments to government boards and corporations to maintain party unity.

articles.headline: Heavy Rainfall Eases Drinking Water Concerns For Bengaluru City
articles.summary: Recent heavy rains in the catchment areas have significantly increased the water levels in Karnataka's four major reservoirs. The inflow has eased concerns about drinking water supplies for Bengaluru and other cities for the coming year.

articles.headline: Karnataka Withdraws AO and AAO Exams After 20 Days Of Protests
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has withdrawn the notification for the recruitment of Agriculture Officers and Assistant Agriculture Officers following 20 days of protests by agriculture graduates. The protesters had demanded revisions to the eligibility criteria.

articles.headline: BDA Citizen-Centric Initiative Wins National Award For Service Excellence
articles.summary: The Bengaluru Development Authority (BDA) has won a national award for its 'Bore Guarantee' initiative, which aims to resolve citizen grievances efficiently. The project was recognized for its transparency and proactive approach to public service.

articles.headline: BEL Signs Memorandum To Explore GIS And GeoAI Defence Solutions
articles.summary: Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) has signed an MoU with Esri India to develop and deploy GIS and GeoAI solutions for the Indian defense forces. The partnership aims to enhance situational awareness and strategic planning through advanced mapping technology.

articles.headline: Minister Directs GPS To Prevent Sale Of Plaster Of Paris Idols
articles.summary: Karnataka's Environment Minister has instructed gram panchayats to ensure that only eco-friendly clay idols are sold for the upcoming Ganesha Chaturthi festival. The move aims to prevent water pollution caused by non-biodegradable Plaster of Paris idols.

articles.headline: NIA Makes 25th Arrest In High-Profile Praveen Nettaru Murder Investigation
articles.summary: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has arrested another individual in connection with the murder of BJP worker Praveen Nettaru. This marks the 25th arrest in the case, which involves alleged members of a banned organization.

articles.headline: Man Caught At Bengaluru Railway Station With Ganja-Infused Chocolates
articles.summary: The Railway Protection Force (RPF) in Bengaluru arrested a man for carrying 19.2 kg of chocolates infused with ganja. The suspect was apprehended during a routine security check and faces charges under the NDPS Act.

articles.headline: Rain Disruption Hits Coal Supply And Karnataka's Thermal Power Generation
articles.summary: Heavy rainfall has disrupted coal supply chains and flooded mines, impacting thermal power generation in Karnataka. The state is facing a power deficit as hydro and solar generation are also currently lower than expected.

articles.headline: Centre Argues Against Excluding SC and ST Creamy Layer From Quotas
articles.summary: The Indian government has told the Supreme Court that the 'creamy layer' concept should not apply to SC and ST reservations. The government argued that these communities still face historical marginalization that justifies uniform quota benefits.

articles.headline: Gold Loan Portfolios Surge 135 Percent Over The Last Three Years
articles.summary: Data from the Ministry of Finance shows that outstanding gold loans of scheduled commercial banks surged from Rs 6.2 lakh crore in 2022-23 to Rs 14.6 lakh crore in 2025-26. The 135% increase highlights a growing reliance on gold as collateral.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Rules Against Punitive Compulsory Retirement For Employees
articles.summary: The Supreme Court stated that compulsory retirement should not be used as a punitive measure against employees unless there is evidence of poor performance or a lack of integrity. The ruling came during a case involving a CISF officer.

articles.headline: CBI Chargesheets Several Bank Officials In Major Fraud Investigation
articles.summary: The CBI has filed chargesheets against multiple bank officials for their alleged involvement in a large-scale financial fraud. The officials are accused of sanctioning fraudulent loans and aiding money laundering activities for private developers.

articles.headline: Six Killed After House Collapses Due To Heavy Rain In Uttar Pradesh
articles.summary: Six members of a family, including children, were killed when their 100-year-old house collapsed during heavy rains in UP's Pratapgarh district. One survivor is currently being treated for serious injuries sustained during the incident.

articles.headline: Dabur Challenges FSSAI Ban On 100 Percent Pure Claims For Honey
articles.summary: Dabur has approached the High Court challenging an FSSAI order that bans the company from claiming its honey is '100% pure.' The company argues that its product meets all safety and quality standards set by the regulator.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi Supports Jharkhand Student Protests Via Social Media Outreach
articles.summary: Rahul Gandhi voiced support for students in Jharkhand protesting against alleged recruitment exam irregularities. During an Instagram live session, he called for a fair investigation and reforms to the state's examination system.

articles.headline: RSS Chief Bhagwat Calls For Education Spending To Reach Six Percent
articles.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat advocated for increasing government spending on education to 6% of the national budget. He emphasized the need for structural reforms to make education more inclusive and focused on traditional family values.

articles.headline: Foreign Funding To Indian NGOs Increases Despite Stricter FCRA Regulations
articles.summary: Despite tighter rules and the cancellation of thousands of licenses, foreign funding to Indian NGOs reached over Rs 55,000 crore between 2021 and 2024. Most funding currently flows to organizations registered under the new FCRA norms.

articles.headline: New Government Rules Require Rapid Removal Of Unlawful Online Posts
articles.summary: The Indian government has issued new guidelines requiring social media platforms to remove unlawful or flagged content within three hours. The rules aim to quickly curb the spread of misinformation and sexually explicit deepfakes.

articles.headline: Britain Faces Rising NEET Problem Among Youth Not In Training
articles.summary: Reports indicate that over 1 in 8 young people in Britain are currently not in education, employment, or training (NEET). The trend is prompting calls for a focus on technical skills and vocational education to address the growing labor gap.

articles.headline: Climate Change Increases Clear Air Turbulence Risks For Global Aviation
articles.summary: Scientific studies show that rising global temperatures are significantly increasing the frequency and severity of clear-air turbulence. This phenomenon poses a growing safety risk for air travel, as it is difficult for conventional radar to detect.

articles.headline: Donald Trump Denies Munitions Shortage and Warns Against Arsenal Leaks
articles.summary: Donald Trump denied reports of a massive munitions shortage in the US military, calling the claims 'fake news.' He warned that those leaking information about national defense stocks would be held accountable for undermining security.

articles.headline: US Tightens Immigration Rules To Allow Outright Denial Of Petitions
articles.summary: New US immigration policies give officers the power to deny visa petitions without first requesting additional evidence. The policy aims to reduce backlogs and discourage the filing of incomplete or fraudulent applications.

articles.headline: New Solar Images Reveal Surfaces Of The Sun In Finest Detail
articles.summary: The Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope has captured unprecedented images of the Sun's surface, showing structures as small as 20 km in diameter. The data will help scientists better understand solar activity and its impact on Earth.

articles.headline: Patient Dies During Chinese Biotech Company Gene Editing Clinical Trial
articles.summary: A patient participating in a gene-editing trial for muscular dystrophy in China has died, raising concerns about the safety of CRISPR-based therapies. Authorities have launched an investigation into the company's experimental protocols.

articles.headline: Akasa Air Plans To Raise 110 Million Dollars Amid Rising Costs
articles.summary: Akasa Air's founder stated the airline is looking to raise $110 million in fresh capital to manage increasing operating costs and fuel prices. The airline plans to expand its fleet to 40 aircraft by the end of the current fiscal year.

articles.headline: Finance Minister Indicates Custom Duty Lowering Possible In Next Budget
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman hinted that the government may consider lowering custom duties on several items in the next budget. The goal is to reduce production costs for domestic manufacturers and boost exports.

articles.headline: Nazara Technologies CEO-Designate Invests 583 Crore In The Company
articles.summary: The incoming CEO of Nazara Technologies, Raymond Albaladejo, has invested Rs 583 crore to acquire a significant stake in the gaming firm. The investment reflects confidence in the company's long-term growth and expansion into global markets.

articles.headline: Microsoft Launches Its Fourth Indian Cloud Data Center Region In Hyderabad
articles.summary: Microsoft has officially launched its fourth cloud region in India, located in Hyderabad. The new facility will provide high-speed cloud services and data residency for local businesses, supporting the country's growing digital economy.

articles.headline: India Cricket Team Struggles Against Spin Bowling In Sri Lanka Series
articles.summary: The Indian cricket team faces mounting pressure after suffering consecutive losses to spin bowling during the ODI series in Sri Lanka. Senior players and the coaching staff are under scrutiny for their inability to handle turning tracks.

articles.headline: Mitchell Starc Humbled To Equal Kapil Dev's Test Wicket Tally
articles.summary: Australian pacer Mitchell Starc expressed humility after equaling Kapil Dev's career total of 434 Test wickets. Starc reached the milestone during the ongoing series, cementing his status as one of the game's greatest left-arm fast bowlers.

articles.headline: India's Mental Conditioning Coach Uses AI To Overcome Language Barriers
articles.summary: Paddy Upton, the mental conditioning coach for the Indian cricket team, is using an AI-powered translation tool to communicate with players in regional languages. The tool allows him to provide real-time psychological support during matches.

articles.headline: Bihar Authorities Order Probe Into Use Of Carton As Medical Splint
articles.summary: The Bihar health department has ordered an inquiry after images of a patient with a cardboard carton used as a leg splint went viral. The incident at a government hospital has drawn widespread criticism over the lack of basic medical equipment.

articles.headline: Atiq Ahmed's Youngest Son Killed In High Speed Car Crash
articles.summary: Ahaan Ahmed, the youngest son of the late gangster-politician Atiq Ahmed, was killed in a high-speed car crash in Uttar Pradesh. The vehicle reportedly hit a divider and overturned, resulting in the death of the 23-year-old and two others.

articles.headline: Varanasi To Be First Non-English Film Shot Entirely In IMAX
articles.summary: Filmmaker SS Rajamouli announced that his upcoming film 'Varanasi' will be the first non-English movie shot entirely using IMAX cameras. The project is expected to set a new standard for high-resolution cinematography in Indian cinema.

articles.headline: Divya Spandana Calls For Menopause To Be Recognized As Public Health Issue
articles.summary: Actor and former MP Divya Spandana has urged the Karnataka government to include menopause support in the state's public health policies. She highlighted that many women suffer in silence due to a lack of awareness and affordable treatment.

articles.headline: Tabu Files Personality Rights Petition In Delhi High Court Against Deepfakes
articles.summary: Actor Tabu has approached the Delhi High Court seeking to protect her personality rights from being exploited by AI-generated deepfakes. The petition calls for a ban on the unauthorized use of her voice and image for commercial purposes.

articles.headline: Anya Taylor-Joy Discusses The Challenges Of Method Acting In New Interview
articles.summary: In a recent interview, actor Anya Taylor-Joy shared her thoughts on the mental toll of intense character roles. She stated that while commitment is necessary, 'losing one's mind' to a role is unsustainable for long-term health and creativity.

articles.headline: Handloom Heritage Takes Centre Stage At Bengaluru Weekend Events
articles.summary: Several exhibitions and workshops celebrating traditional Indian handlooms are scheduled across Bengaluru this weekend. The events aim to promote sustainable fashion and support local artisans from various regions of the country.

articles.headline: JSW Steel and Tata Steel pursue contrasting growth strategies
articles.summary: JSW Steel aims to double capacity to 80 million tonnes by 2031 through joint ventures and greenfield projects. In contrast, Tata Steel is prioritizing higher-margin downstream products like precision tubes and specialty wires. JSW focuses on global scale, while Tata Steel believes relentless capacity addition is unnecessary, focusing instead on value-added portfolio expansion.

articles.headline: FSSAI intensifies crackdown on misleading food and beverage labels
articles.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is increasing enforcement against FMCG brands making misleading packaging claims. Recent actions against Dabur and United Spirits have led to legal challenges. The regulator is using social media and mobile apps to allow consumers to report violations. The move follows criticism that Indian food standards lag behind Europe.

articles.headline: Over one-third of eligible Indian companies fail to file annual returns
articles.summary: More than 664,000 companies failed to file annual returns or financial statements in 2024-25. Legal experts warn the corporate registry is becoming cluttered with inactive or financially stressed firms, undermining data reliability for investors. Compliance has deteriorated over five years despite a surge in registered companies. Enforcement actions remain low compared to defaults.

articles.headline: RBI raises FY27 GDP growth forecast while lowering inflation outlook
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% in its August meeting. The central bank raised its FY27 GDP growth forecast to 6.7% from 6.6%. Simultaneously, it lowered the consumer price index inflation estimate to 5.0% from 5.1%. However, an increase in the Q4 inflation forecast to 5.5% suggests the possibility of future rate hikes remains open.

articles.headline: Indian banks mobilize 28 billion dollars in foreign currency deposits
articles.summary: Banks raised approximately $28 billion in net fresh foreign currency non-resident (FCNR) deposits between June and July 2026. This surge followed an RBI incentive scheme designed to attract foreign currency and support the rupee. HSBC, State Bank of India, and ICICI Bank accounted for nearly half the inflows. Private sector banks led the mobilization with $10.7 billion.

articles.headline: India records lowest Commonwealth Games medal haul since 1998
articles.summary: India finished fourth at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games with 39 medals, including 14 gold, 16 silver, and nine bronze. This was the country's lowest tally in nearly three decades, primarily due to the inclusion of only 10 sports and the exclusion of disciplines where India historically excels. Australia topped the table with 171 medals, followed by England and Canada.

articles.headline: Urad prices expected to remain stable despite El Nino concerns
articles.summary: India is confident in comfortable urad supplies as sowing is 11% higher than last year, defying broader kharif acreage declines. Adequate imports from Myanmar and Brazil are expected to supplement domestic production. The consumer affairs department predicts stable supplies will keep a lid on related food inflation for items like idli, dosa, and dal makhani.

articles.headline: Parliament passes Taxation and Other Laws Amendment Bill 2026
articles.summary: The Lok Sabha passed legislation to fine-tune the country's tax and payments architecture, while the Rajya Sabha approved the Appropriation Bill for additional government spending. The amendments to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act may allow banks to charge merchant discount rate fees on large UPI transactions in the future, aligning with new regulatory requirements.

articles.headline: RITES develops standard-gauge diesel locomotives to boost global exports
articles.summary: State-run RITES is developing a standard-gauge version of Indian Railways' diesel locomotives to target markets in Australia, Europe, and the Americas. The strategy aims to monetize surplus diesel fleet as India electrifies its network. A prototype is currently being developed for an Australian customer. The move leverages the 10-15 years of remaining life in India's diesel engines.

articles.headline: Private equity firm KKR acquires Medicover’s Indian hospital operations
articles.summary: KKR has acquired the Indian operations of Stockholm-based Medicover AB, which includes 24 multi-specialty hospitals and 4,800 beds across South and West India. The investment reflects KKR's confidence in the long-term potential of the Indian healthcare ecosystem. The move comes amid a wave of consolidation where regional players are being acquired by national and global chains.

articles.headline: Shiprocket shifts focus to non-shipping tech services ahead of IPO
articles.summary: Logistics aggregator Shiprocket is betting on cross-border commerce, omnichannel software, and marketing solutions to drive growth. These non-shipping services now generate over 25% of revenue. The company plans to open its ₹1,618-crore IPO on August 12. Proceeds will be used for AI development, acquisitions, and expanding its fulfillment network as it transitions to a tech platform.

articles.headline: LIC reports 23 percent profit growth amid shrinking disposable incomes
articles.summary: Life Insurance Corp. of India (LIC) posted a net profit of ₹13,492 crore for the June quarter, a 23% year-on-year increase. Despite the profit rise, the insurer warned that shrinking household disposable incomes are weighing on premium growth, particularly in the savings segment. Total premium income rose nearly 7% to ₹1.27 trillion, driven by a shift toward higher-margin products.

articles.headline: Stock option traders face delivery risks under new closing auction
articles.summary: Derivative traders could face unexpected physical delivery obligations on monthly stock option expiries due to the newly introduced closing auction session. Because final settlement prices are determined only after the window closes, options may move from out-of-the-money to in-the-money abruptly. This creates a delivery liability that traders may not have hedged against.

articles.headline: Legacy two-wheeler makers revamp organizations for electric and premium shift
articles.summary: Hero MotoCorp, Bajaj Auto, and TVS Motor are restructuring to focus on high-growth electric vehicle (EV) and premium segments. Strategies include creating dedicated leadership roles and expanding exclusive retail networks. EV sales rose 22% to 1.4 million units in FY26. Bajaj plans to reach 1,000 Chetak EV stores, while Hero appointed new heads for premium and emerging mobility units.

articles.headline: Sebi to simplify regulations and leverage technology for market supervision
articles.summary: In its annual report, Sebi announced plans to focus on easing compliance, removing regulatory redundancies, and launching the "Sebi Setu" portal. The regulator will pilot the tokenization of corporate bonds and introduce a fast-track mechanism for AIF schemes. Sebi is also using AI to detect market manipulation and fraud while expanding its regional presence for better monitoring.

articles.headline: Omnivore to deploy remaining capital into deep science and consumer brands
articles.summary: Impact venture capital firm Omnivore plans to invest the balance 45% of its ₹1,800-crore Fund III by mid-2027. Co-founder Mark Kahn stated focus areas include robotics, physical AI, and life sciences that benefit farmers. The firm recently co-led a ₹230-crore round for Arboreal Bio-innovations. Omnivore is positioning itself for a cycle where high-protein foods and deeptech see high demand.

articles.headline: Two Israeli soldiers killed in Lebanon explosion despite shaky truce
articles.summary: The Israeli military reported its first fatalities since a Lebanon ceasefire began two months ago. Two soldiers died and four were seriously wounded in an explosion in southern Lebanon. In response, Israel launched strikes and issued evacuation warnings for the village of Mansouri. Lebanon's Health Ministry reported one death and several injuries following retaliatory Israeli strikes.

articles.headline: OpenAI prioritizes Indic language performance and voice AI for India
articles.summary: OpenAI is making Indic language performance a research priority to better serve the Indian startup ecosystem. The move follows feedback from founders regarding the need for better voice AI in local languages. India is considered one of the most vibrant AI markets globally. The firm aims to lower costs and improve tools for B2B customers in sectors where voice is the primary interface.

articles.headline: Korean giant Hybe hunts for members of first Indian girl group
articles.summary: Hybe Corp, the agency behind BTS, has established a Mumbai office and begun auditions for an all-girl band in India. The group will be built using K-pop training principles but will feature Indian identity and authenticity. Hybe aims to replicate its global success by cultivating a loyal fandom in India, leveraging digital platforms like Weverse for direct artiste-fan engagement.

articles.headline: West Asia conflict inflicts steep raw material cost shock on firms
articles.summary: The West Asia conflict has pushed raw material prices up by 45% year-on-year in the June quarter, more than the Russia-Ukraine war. This has squeezed corporate profit margins to three-year lows. Chemicals, paints, and auto ancillary sectors are particularly affected. However, investments in captive renewable energy have helped some firms absorb parts of the energy cost spike.

articles.headline: BEE to review Bharat Vecto tool for commercial vehicle fuel efficiency
articles.summary: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) will periodically review Bharat Vecto, a tool simulating real-world Indian road conditions to test truck fuel efficiency. The tool, developed by ARAI, is intended to replace current testing protocols. Automakers prefer this simulation over track tests at constant speeds. The first phase for diesel vehicles is planned for launch by December 2026.

articles.headline: Parliament passes bill to increase sanctioned strength of Supreme Court judges
articles.summary: Parliament has passed the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill 2026. The legislation increases the sanctioned strength of judges from 33 to 37, excluding the Chief Justice of India. The expansion aims to address the growing backlog of cases and improve the efficiency of the apex court. This is the first increase in judge strength since 2019.

articles.headline: India’s non-fossil fuel electricity capacity crosses 300 gigawatt mark
articles.summary: Union Minister Pralhad Joshi announced that India’s non-fossil fuel electricity generation capacity has surpassed 300 GW. The nation added over 30 GW of renewable capacity between January and June. India remains on track to achieve its target of 500 GW of renewable energy by 2030. The growth is driven by massive investments in solar and wind projects across the country.

articles.headline: Rupee falls 14 paise to close at record low against dollar
articles.summary: The Indian rupee depreciated by 14 paise to close at 95.22 against the US dollar. The decline was triggered by a recovery in the US Dollar Index and rising US Treasury yields. Foreign fund outflows also pressured the domestic currency, despite lower global crude oil prices providing some support. The rupee traded in a range of 95.12 to 95.24 during the session.

articles.headline: RBI defers implementation of new loan recovery guidelines to January 2027
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has extended the deadline for banks to implement stricter loan recovery guidelines by three months. The rules, now effective January 1, 2027, bar recovery agents from using harsh tactics, abusive language, or calling borrowers outside prescribed hours. The deferral follows requests from the banking industry to allow more time for operational changes.

articles.headline: IMD warns of heavy rainfall and flash floods across northern India
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued warnings for heavy rainfall and localized flash floods in Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu over the next week. Flash flood risks are high in mountainous regions. The rain is expected to persist across north-west, central, and north-eastern India, impacting kharif crop activities and local transport.

articles.headline: Niti Aayog calls for easing land acquisition to attract industrial investment
articles.summary: Niti Aayog Vice Chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri emphasized that India needs to simplify land acquisition processes for industries to boost investment. Addressing a policy forum, he noted that land availability remains a significant hurdle for setting up manufacturing units. The reform is considered crucial for India's goal of becoming a developed economy by 2047.

articles.headline: Centre raises apprenticeship target to 600,000 students for fiscal 2027
articles.summary: The Central government has increased its apprenticeship target under the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme by 40% for FY27. The goal is to enroll 600,000 students, supported by an allocation of ₹1,250 crore. The initiative aims to bridge the skill gap and improve employability for youth, aligning with the "Viksit Bharat" vision for industrial growth.

articles.headline: NRIs face complex tax and repatriation rules in Indian property deals
articles.summary: Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) selling property in India must navigate a maze of FEMA regulations and tax requirements. Key considerations include the $1 million annual repatriation limit from NRO accounts and mandatory TDS deductions of 12.5% on capital gains. Experts advise using specific power of attorney and ensuring PAN card availability to avoid transaction delays and penalties.

articles.headline: Sebi proposes bigger role for clearing corporations in risk management
articles.summary: Market regulator Sebi has proposed shifting more operational responsibility for settlement and risk management to clearing corporations. A new consultation paper suggests clearing corporations should solely monitor pay-in shortages and collect penalties, duties currently split with stock exchanges. The proposal aims to streamline operations and reduce compliance burdens for brokers.

articles.headline: Biocon views proposed US generic drug tariffs as negotiation tactic
articles.summary: Biocon executive chairperson Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw stated that proposed US tariffs on imported generics are likely a "negotiating threat" rather than a real risk. She argued that such tariffs would contradict US efforts to lower healthcare costs. Biocon remains in wait-and-watch mode but is exploring US manufacturing partnerships via Syngene if local production becomes mandatory.

articles.headline: Experts emphasize storage and transmission for India’s green energy transition
articles.summary: At the Mint Sustainability Summit, stakeholders highlighted that India's next phase of energy transition depends on expanding transmission infrastructure and large-scale battery storage. While renewable capacity is growing, the grid remains a bottleneck. Experts called for greater transparency regarding capacity delays and the adoption of green hydrogen in refineries and fertilizers.

articles.headline: Bisleri CEO warns India’s water crisis is management issue not rainfall
articles.summary: Bisleri International CEO Angelo George stated that India’s water scarcity is a result of poor governance rather than lack of rain. Speaking at a summit, he noted per capita water availability has dropped 75% in 70 years. The company is building rainwater harvesting infrastructure and check dams to mitigate risks, while advocating for a "water credit" market to reward conservation.

articles.headline: Youth protests have as much to do with jobs as leaks
articles.summary: Recent youth protests in Delhi regarding exam paper leaks highlight growing anxiety over India's employment situation. While unemployment rates are falling, real earnings for regular jobs have stagnated. Many graduates find themselves in insecure roles without social security or written contracts. Experts argue the system needs to create more jobs that offer a decent living wage.

articles.headline: Let UPI pay for itself to sustain India’s digital infrastructure
articles.summary: Proposals to allow banks to charge fees on large UPI transactions follow the user-pays principle applied to other infrastructure. While UPI achieved high penetration as a free service, recovering operational costs is essential for continued investment. The government currently subsidizes low-value transactions, but long-term sustainability may require transparent usage charges.

articles.headline: Why nobody expected the MPC to increase interest rates this week
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank's decision to keep the repo rate unchanged was expected by markets despite rising inflation. RBI is increasingly seen as favoring wait-and-watch strategies rather than preemptive tightening. Markets infer a hierarchy where protecting the rupee and supporting growth may currently outweigh strict adherence to the 4% inflation target during periods of global volatility.

articles.headline: Upper Assam floods reveal outdated financial set-up for disaster response
articles.summary: Devastating floods in Upper Assam reveal a policy mismatch between disaster risk and adaptive capacity. While funding has increased under the Finance Commission, the infrastructure often fails during deluges. Effective mitigation requires cross-border cooperation between states as rivers transcend administrative boundaries. Funding models should be proactive rather than based on past data.

articles.headline: AI movies show potential for human connection beyond digital slop
articles.summary: The AI film festival in Tokyo showcased shorts that emanated genuine human emotion, challenging the view that AI-generated art is soulless. While concerns over intellectual property and labor remain, technology can empower artists to tell complex stories on limited budgets. Ultimately, audiences will decide based on the quality of storytelling rather than the tools used during production.

articles.headline: India ought to resolve current asymmetry in its GST regime deadlines
articles.summary: Legal experts argue that the GST regime is starkly rigid when taxpayers miss deadlines while the state frequently grants itself extensions for compliance issues. Adjudicating authorities currently lack the discretion to condone delays for sufficient cause, unlike in direct tax laws. Providing appellate forums the latitude to consider genuine hardship would support small businesses.

articles.headline: MDR of less than 0.25% on P2M UPI deals can compensate stakeholders
articles.summary: A Finance Ministry study suggests that a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) of less than 0.25% on person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions could adequately compensate banks and payment service providers without burdening consumers.

articles.headline: Share of fresher hires in IT drops to 24% in July
articles.summary: Hiring of freshers in India's technology sector fell from 32% to 24% year-on-year in July 2026. Conversely, the share of experienced professionals grew, reflecting a shift in industry hiring trends towards skilled expertise.

articles.headline: KKR signs deal with Medicover to acquire India arm for $1.5b
articles.summary: Global investment firm KKR has agreed to acquire the Indian operations of healthcare and diagnostic service provider Medicover for $1.5 billion (₹14,280 crore) to expand its footprint in the domestic healthcare sector.

articles.headline: Capex by 59 CPSEs tops 33% of FY27 target in April-July
articles.summary: Capital expenditure by 59 central public sector enterprises and four government entities reached ₹2.82 lakh crore in the first four months of FY27, achieving 33.5% of their annual target. The Railway Board led spending at ₹1.19 lakh crore.

articles.headline: MDR will be only for merchants, not UPI users, clarifies FM
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman clarified that the proposed Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) will only apply to merchants and not to UPI end users. The government aims to protect common people from costs while supporting infrastructure.

articles.headline: Auto retail sales soar 26% in record July: FADA
articles.summary: Indian automobile retail sales grew 26% year-on-year in July 2026, reaching a record 25.91 lakh units. Growth was reported across all segments, including two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, and commercial vehicles.

articles.headline: TN Agri Budget mixes tradition with modernised farming
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government presented its maiden Agriculture Budget for 2026-27, focusing on soil fertility, organic farming, and AI-driven precision agriculture to shift the state's economic focus back to the primary sector.

articles.headline: India must seek exemption from US tariffs for key sectors
articles.summary: A parliamentary panel recommended that India negotiate exemptions from future US Section 301 tariffs for key exports like pharmaceuticals and critical minerals to protect domestic trade interests and market competitiveness.

articles.headline: Biocon bets on new US drugs for stronger H2
articles.summary: Biocon expects a stronger second half of FY27 as recently launched biosimilars in the US, including Yesafili and Opuviz, begin to contribute significantly to its revenue. The company is focusing on high-growth R&D products.

articles.headline: Reliance Power Q1 PAT jumps 44% to ₹65 crore
articles.summary: Reliance Power reported a 44% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to ₹65 crore for the first quarter of FY27. Operating performance improved despite ongoing legal and financial challenges at some subsidiaries.

articles.headline: Britannia Industries Q1 PAT up 14% to ₹593 crore
articles.summary: Britannia Industries posted a 14% rise in Q1 net profit to ₹593 crore, supported by healthy volume growth and strong traction in e-commerce. Consolidated sales for the quarter rose 9.5% to ₹4,964 crore.

articles.headline: CCPA slaps ₹20 lakh fine on FirstCry, Zepto, and others
articles.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority imposed penalties of ₹20 lakh on seven e-commerce platforms, including Zepto and FirstCry, for using 'dark patterns' to manipulate consumer choices and basket sneaking.

articles.headline: Centre spent over ₹187 crore on PM Modi’s foreign visits
articles.summary: The Indian government spent ₹187.83 crore on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 14 foreign visits in 2025. This reflects a significant increase from previous years as international engagements resumed fully post-pandemic.

articles.headline: Pidilite passes on raw material cost impact, profit rises 30%
articles.summary: Pidilite Industries reported a 30% rise in Q1 net profit to ₹884 crore by passing on increased raw material costs to consumers. Consolidated revenue grew 21% to ₹4,551 crore driven by sustained demand.

articles.headline: Dabur watchful of headwinds, targets double-digit growth in FY27
articles.summary: Dabur India is aiming for double-digit growth in FY27 despite geopolitical tensions and raw material cost pressures. The company plans to maintain a balance between pricing and volume growth in its core segments.

articles.headline: Dabur moves court against FSSAI’s prohibition order
articles.summary: Dabur India has approached the Delhi High Court challenging an FSSAI order that prohibited the sale of some of its food products over labeling issues. The company maintains its products meet all safety standards.

articles.headline: Trent’s Q1 profit jumps 26%, revenue hits ₹5,666 crore
articles.summary: Tata-owned retailer Trent reported a 26% rise in first-quarter net profit to ₹518 crore. Revenue grew 19% to ₹5,666 crore, driven by aggressive store expansion for its Zudio and Westside fashion brands.

articles.headline: Emami Agrotech eyes snacking market with ₹750 crore investment
articles.summary: Emami Agrotech plans to invest ₹750 crore over the next few years to enter the branded packaged snack market. The company will focus on high-margin products targeting younger generations across India.

articles.headline: Lumina Datamatics closes acquisition of TNQTech
articles.summary: Lumina Datamatics has completed the acquisition of Chennai-based publishing technology firm TNQTech. The deal aims to enhance Lumina's AI-powered content services and expand its reach in the scholarly publishing market.

articles.headline: Closing price gap narrows for Nifty as markets adapt
articles.summary: The difference between the Nifty's standard closing price and the post-auction session price narrowed significantly to 8 points. Traders are successfully adapting to the new Closing Auction Session (CAS) mechanism introduced by NSE.

articles.headline: SEBI mulls single-window relief outreach and Jagrook initiatives
articles.summary: SEBI Chairperson Madhabi Puri Buch announced an AI-enabled multilingual investor awareness campaign and simplified nomination norms for demat accounts. The regulator also plans a fast-track mechanism for processing AIF applications.

articles.headline: Shiprocket sets IPO price at ₹92-97, opens Aug 12
articles.summary: E-commerce logistics firm Shiprocket has fixed its IPO price band at ₹92-97 per share, aiming to raise ₹1,617.48 crore. The public offer will open for subscription on August 12 and close on August 14.

articles.headline: MV Electrosystems and Juniper Green see strong listing gains
articles.summary: MV Electrosystems and Juniper Green Energy made strong debuts on the stock exchanges, with shares listing at premiums of 47% and 15% respectively over their IPO prices, reflecting positive investor sentiment.

articles.headline: Milky Mist IPO price band fixed at ₹133-140
articles.summary: Milky Mist Dairy Food has set an IPO price band of ₹133-140 per share for its ₹1,553 crore public offer. The issue is scheduled to open for subscription on August 11 and close on August 13.

articles.headline: Govt may rationalise most customs tariff by FY28 Budget
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman indicated the government might rationalise most customs tariffs by the FY2027-28 budget to boost domestic manufacturing and competitiveness, though progress is currently being made sector by sector.

articles.headline: India and South Africa discuss preferential trade pact
articles.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal met with SACU counterparts to discuss a potential preferential trade agreement. The talks focused on strengthening economic ties and expanding market access in sectors like pharmaceuticals and minerals.

articles.headline: India rules out concessions to US on ethanol imports
articles.summary: India has stated it will not offer concessions on ethanol imports for fuel blending, as its blending program is driven by domestic policy and indigenous feedstock. The clarification comes amid ongoing bilateral trade negotiations.

articles.headline: Syrma SGS sharpens original design manufacturing capabilities
articles.summary: Syrma SGS is expanding its original design manufacturing (ODM) capabilities to drive growth in medical and defense electronics. The company aims for higher margins and increased export contributions through tech-led design.

articles.headline: Indian Bank approves ₹505 crore MSME loans
articles.summary: As part of its 120th Foundation Day celebrations, Indian Bank approved MSME loans worth ₹505 crore during a credit outreach program. The bank aims to strengthen its support for small and medium businesses nationwide.

articles.headline: Higher GST for kraft paper irks corrugated box makers
articles.summary: Manufacturers are protesting the increase in GST on kraft paper from 12% to 18%, while the tax on finished corrugated boxes remains at 5%. The industry warns of financial strain and increased borrowing costs due to the disparity.

articles.headline: RBI issues comprehensive loan recovery rules for protection
articles.summary: The RBI has issued strict new rules for loan recovery, prohibiting lenders from contacting borrowers outside of 8 am to 7 pm or using abusive language. The move aims to protect borrowers from harassment by recovery agents.

articles.headline: Ola Electric pivots to dealer-led retail after five years
articles.summary: Ola Electric is transitioning from its company-owned store model to a dealer-led retail and service network across India. The move aims to scale its presence in smaller towns and enhance customer support through local partners.

articles.headline: Global sugar prices poised to rule lower this quarter
articles.summary: Global sugar prices are expected to decline this quarter due to improved production forecasts in Brazil and higher stocks in Thailand and the US. This follows a period of high prices driven by El Nino concerns.

articles.headline: ISMA, sugar mills seek sops to offset crushing losses
articles.summary: The Indian Sugar and Bio-energy Manufacturers Association has requested government support to offset losses expected from an early start to the crushing season. Mills are seeking higher MSP and GST waivers on domestic sales.

articles.headline: Kerala braces for renewed monsoon fury as IMD warns
articles.summary: The IMD has issued a warning for intense rainfall in Kerala and southern Karnataka over the next few days. The state has initiated safety protocols to mitigate potential flooding and damage from heavy downpours.

articles.headline: Daily rooftop solar installations under PM Surya Ghar cross 16,300
articles.summary: Installations under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana have exceeded 16,300 per day. The scheme has already benefited over 12 lakh households, adding 14 gigawatts of cumulative rooftop solar capacity across India.

articles.headline: Karnataka explores long-term AI partnership with Anthropic
articles.summary: The Karnataka government is discussing a partnership with AI firm Anthropic to integrate advanced AI solutions into governance, health, and education. The initiative aims to build a robust and responsible AI ecosystem in the state.

articles.headline: Govt pushes to pass FCRA amendment Bill this session
articles.summary: The government is working to pass the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, before the current session ends. The Bill aims to introduce stricter controls on the receipt and utilization of foreign donations.

articles.headline: Centre approves ₹8,970 crore Guwahati-Tezpur corridor
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet has approved ₹8,970 crore for a 124-km four-lane access-controlled highway in Assam. The project includes 15 major bridges and aims to improve regional connectivity and travel speeds significantly.

articles.headline: TRAI’s 5G slicing norms convoluted, say telecom experts
articles.summary: Industry analysts warn that TRAI's new 5G network slicing guidelines could hurt regular users by prioritizing premium services, potentially leading to increased congestion and degraded service quality for the general public.

articles.headline: FDA approves first mRNA flu shot from Moderna
articles.summary: The US FDA has approved the first mRNA-based seasonal flu vaccine, developed by Moderna, for adults aged 50 and older. This marks a significant milestone in expanding mRNA technology beyond Covid-19 applications.

articles.headline: Govt cuts online content takedown time to 2 hours
articles.summary: New government regulations have reduced the mandatory time for social media platforms to remove illegal or sensitive online content to just two hours. This amendment aims to address rapid misinformation spread and harmful content.

articles.headline: Iran warns Gulf states: Tell Trump to desist or hit hard
articles.summary: Iran has issued a diplomatic warning via Gulf states, explicitly stating that Tehran will target their oil facilities and power plants if they allow their territory or airspace to be used for US strikes on Iran. Senior Iranian officials told their Arab counterparts that any attack on Iran would prompt immediate retaliation against local infrastructure to prevent wider escalation.

articles.headline: Tejpal convicted, given 10-year jail in 2013 rape case
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court's Goa bench convicted former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal of raping a junior colleague in 2013, overturning a 2021 trial court acquittal. The court sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment, ruling that the prosecution had proved the charges beyond reasonable doubt. Tejpal has been given four weeks to surrender to the authorities.

articles.headline: Netanyahu dials Modi, discusses W Asia situation
articles.summary: Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called Prime Minister Narendra Modi to review the ongoing situation in West Asia and bilateral relations. PM Modi reaffirmed India's commitment to finding a lasting solution to the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy while expressing concern over the current regional instability. They also discussed ways to strengthen the strategic partnership.

articles.headline: Gen Z grievances genuine, says RSS chief
articles.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat stated that the grievances of Gen Z are genuine and should be addressed through dialogue. Speaking at an event, he emphasized that young protesters should not be labeled anti-national for expressing concerns over issues like unemployment and reservations. He called for improvements in India's education policy and inclusive development that includes the LGBTQIA+ community.

articles.headline: RBI retains Tata Sons in upper layer NBFC list
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has retained Tata Sons Pvt Ltd in the upper layer of non-banking financial companies (NBFCs-UL) for FY27. This decision means the company must continue to comply with enhanced regulatory requirements. Tata Sons had sought to surrender its core investment company registration to avoid being listed as an upper-layer NBFC, but the RBI has maintained its status for now.

articles.headline: Cabinet approves 23,700 crore rupee scheme for compressed biogas sector
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet cleared a ₹23,731-crore GOBARdhan scheme to boost India's compressed biogas (CBG) production. The initiative, running from FY27 to FY36, aims to increase domestic production ten-fold. It addresses infrastructure hurdles and promotes sustainable waste-to-energy solutions. The scheme is a key component of India's strategy to reduce fuel imports and achieve net-zero targets.

articles.headline: Three seek to turn approver in Renukaswamy murder
articles.summary: Three accused in the Renukaswamy murder case have approached a Bengaluru court seeking to become approvers. This move could significantly strengthen the prosecution's case against other accused, including Kannada actor Darshan. The court has reserved its order on whether their testimony can be recorded before the trial begins. Seventeen people have been arrested in the case so far.

articles.headline: TN unveils Rs 58,374 cr agriculture budget, focus on El Nino
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Minister M.R.K. Paneerselvam presented a Rs 58,374 crore agri budget for FY 2026-27, with a special focus on mitigating the impact of El Nino on farming. The budget includes Rs 3,600 crore for a new Soil Fertility Mission and funds for micro-irrigation. It also leverages AI and machine learning for pest control and crop yield prediction to boost farmer income.

articles.headline: Agni-4 ballistic missile test fired successfully
articles.summary: India successfully test-fired the intermediate-range ballistic missile Agni-4 from the Chandipur integrated test range off the Odisha coast. The Strategic Forces Command conducted the launch, which validated all operational and technical parameters. The Agni-4 has a range of approximately 4,000 km and is a key component of India's nuclear deterrence strategy.

articles.headline: Health ministry notifies stricter pharmaceutical drug rules
articles.summary: The Union Health Ministry has notified stricter rules for pharmaceutical companies to ensure data integrity and transparency. The amended Drugs and Cosmetics Rules now mandate companies to submit verifiable data for drug approvals. Companies found submitting fake or fabricated data will face cancellation of licenses and can be barred from filing new applications for a specified period.

articles.headline: LIC Q1 profit rises 23% to Rs 13,492 cr
articles.summary: Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) reported a 23% increase in its net profit for the first quarter of the current fiscal year, reaching Rs 13,492 crore. The insurer's total income grew to Rs 2.22 lakh crore, driven by strong growth in group business and renewal premiums. LIC remains the dominant player in the Indian life insurance market with a significant share of new business.

articles.headline: France Submits Official Proposal For 114 Rafale Fighter Jets To India
articles.summary: France has submitted a commercial proposal for 114 Rafale fighter jets to the Indian government. The proposed deal includes 94 jets to be manufactured in India under a strategic partnership, with the remaining 20 supplied directly from France.

articles.headline: Lok Sabha Nod To Bill Permitting Charges On UPI Transactions
articles.summary: The Lok Sabha passed a bill that allows the government to permit banks and fintech companies to charge for certain UPI transactions. The move is intended to ensure the long-term sustainability of the digital payments infrastructure.

articles.headline: Google AI veterans depart as Demis Hassabis moves to chairman role
articles.summary: Google is restructuring its AI leadership following the departure of veteran Jeff Dean, who is launching a startup. Demis Hassabis will transition to chairman of Google DeepMind and chief scientist of Alphabet. Koray Kavukcuoglu has been promoted to lead DeepMind's operations. The overhaul comes as Google faces intense competition from OpenAI and seeks to accelerate its Gemini AI models.

articles.headline: Coal India enters iron ore mining as preferred bidder in Odisha
articles.summary: State-owned Coal India Ltd (CIL) has emerged as the top bidder for the Gadadharpur iron ore block in Odisha, quoting a 114% premium. This marks CIL's first foray into iron ore mining, diversifying away from coal. The block holds an estimated 258 million tonnes of resources. The move aligns with the government's goal to reach a national steel capacity of 300 million tonnes by 2030.

articles.headline: Iran and Oman reach principle agreement on Strait of Hormuz shipping
articles.summary: Iran and Oman have agreed in principle on a plan to manage maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The deal covers entry and exit routes and could be valid for up to four months. While not a full reopening, the arrangement may facilitate negotiations regarding Iran's nuclear program. The UAE has meanwhile maintained high oil flows by using shuttle runs and dark crossings.

articles.headline: Swiggy targets 10,000 crore rupee Ebitda by fiscal year 2031
articles.summary: IPO-bound Swiggy unveiled a roadmap aiming for ₹10,000 crore in adjusted Ebitda by FY31. The company expects to triple its gross order value to ₹2.5 trillion, driven by food delivery and quick commerce. Swiggy plans to expand its monthly transacting user base to over 40 million. The Instamart segment is nearing Ebitda breakeven, with narrowing contribution margin losses.
